newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 1.7 pct in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 1.7 pct in active trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped an average 1.71 percent in active trade on Tuesday as the market's uptrend continued from Monday amid a positive mood, brokers said.
"An uptrend has started. This is not a (temporary) reaction, there are serious stock purchases," said Seyfullah Esen from Oki securities.
"This uptrend may last for a month and carry the index to 70,000-75,000 range," he added.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 1,125.81 points higher at a day's high of 66,944.77. It had gained 1.6 percent on Monday after last week's 2.1 percent rise.
Trade volume soared to 9.6 trillion lira from 6.9 trillion on Monday.
Brokers said selling was triggered as the index approached stiff resistance at 67,000 twice in the day, but the market managed to rebound to close just below 67,000.
They said lower yields and a heavy demand in today's 189-day t-bill auction contributed to market morale.
Bankers were expecting the Treasury to extend t-bill maturities and lower yields after it successfully launched the first foreign-currency denominated bond sale to Turkish banks.
The Treasury will sell $1.12 billion of the bonds to banks on September 25, aiming to extend maturities and relieve the burden of heavy domestic borrowing on the Turkish lira.

Brokers said easing tensions in the Gulf and newly emerging nine-month profit prospects of companies also buoyed the market after last week's fears caused by fighting in northern Iraq and the U.S. missile strikes on military targets in southern Iraq.

The 85-share industrial index .ISEI leapt 1.91 percent to 73,230.64 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF rose 1.2 percent to 59,731.97. Of the 224 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 124 to 43 and 57 were steady.
Actives were led by utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 4,000 lira at 70,000 and its associate Kepez Elektrik, up 3,000 lira at 73,000. The two stocks made up 19 percent of the total volume.
